question: For Toyota Motor Corporation's FY2027 first quarter (April 1 - June 30, 2026; Toyota's fiscal year ends March 31), what were consolidated operating income and net income attributable to Toyota shareholders in yen, what is the company's revised FY2027 operating income forecast versus its previous (May 2026) forecast, and which line items explain why net income rose strongly while operating income fell?
grading: Key points (all required): (1) Q1 FY2027 operating income about JPY 1,063.5 billion (JPY 1,063,473 million; accept 1,063.4-1,063.5), down 8.8% y/y; (2) net income attributable to Toyota JPY 1,477.0 billion (+75.6%); (3) revised FY2027 operating income forecast JPY 3.4 trillion versus JPY 3.0 trillion previously; (4) explanation: income before income taxes was JPY 1,963.9 billion (+56.8%), about JPY 900 billion above operating income, helped by other finance income (JPY 850.6 billion vs 153.7 billion a year earlier), equity-method profit (JPY 210.7 billion) and a foreign-exchange gain (JPY 112.4 billion vs a JPY 212.4 billion loss), partly offset by other finance costs (JPY 285.6 billion). Fail if the answer states the quarter as calendar 2027 or Jan-Mar, uses the May forecast (JPY 3.0 trillion) as current, or says net income fell.
answer: Q1 FY2027 (April 1-June 30, 2026): sales revenues JPY 13,525.4 billion (+10.4%); operating income JPY 1,063.5 billion (-8.8% from JPY 1,166.1 billion); income before income taxes JPY 1,963.9 billion (+56.8%); net income attributable to Toyota JPY 1,477.0 billion (+75.6%) [W10-E1]. The gap is non-operating: other finance income of JPY 850.6 billion (JPY 153.7 billion a year earlier), equity-method profit JPY 210.7 billion and a JPY 112.4 billion FX gain (vs a JPY 212.4 billion loss), less JPY 285.6 billion of other finance costs [W10-E1]. The FY2027 forecast was raised on 4 August to operating income JPY 3.4 trillion (from JPY 3.0 trillion), net income JPY 3.25 trillion (from 3.0 trillion) and sales JPY 54.0 trillion (from 51.0 trillion), with USD/JPY assumed at 160 (from 150) [W10-E2].

output.answer:
## Toyota FY2027 Q1 (April 1 – June 30, 2026)

**Headline results (IFRS, consolidated)**

| Metric | FY2027 Q1 | YoY change |
|---|---|---|
| Sales revenues | ¥13,525.4 bn | +¥1,272.0 bn (+10.4%) |
| **Operating income** | **¥1,063.473 bn** | **−¥102.6 bn (−8.8%)** |
| Income before income taxes | ¥1,963.862 bn | +¥711.7 bn (+56.8%) |
| **Net income attributable to Toyota Motor Corp.** | **¥1,477.044 bn** | **+¥635.6 bn (+75.6%)** |

Basic EPS attributable to Toyota: ¥120.69 (vs. ¥64.56 a year earlier).

## FY2027 full-year operating income forecast revision

| | FY2026 actual | Previous forecast (May 2026) | Revised forecast (Aug 4, 2026) | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales revenues | ¥50,684.9 bn | ¥51,000.0 bn | **¥54,000.0 bn** | +¥3,000.0 bn |
| **Operating income** | ¥3,766.2 bn | ¥3,000.0 bn | **¥3,400.0 bn** | **+¥400.0 bn** |
| Net income attributable to Toyota | ¥3,848.0 bn | ¥3,000.0 bn | ¥3,250.0 bn | +¥250.0 bn |

The ¥400 bn operating income upgrade reflects changed FX assumptions (weaker yen — now ¥150/US$, €181) plus marketing efforts including newly established alternative logistics routes to the Middle East. Toyota noted the impact of the 2026 Kumamoto earthquake is still under assessment and is **not** reflected in the forecast. Even after the raise, the revised ¥3.4 tn is still −9.7% versus FY2026's ¥3,766.2 bn. It also authorized up to ¥1 tn of share repurchases and the cancellation of 200 million treasury shares.

## Why net income rose sharply while operating income fell

The gap is entirely *below* the operating line — it is not a case of operations improving.

**Operating income walk (why it fell −¥102.6 bn):**
- Marketing efforts: **+¥70.0 bn**
- FX effects: **+¥345.0 bn**
- Cost reduction efforts: **−¥85.0 bn** (engineering −¥90.0 bn; manufacturing/logistics +¥5.0 bn)
- Increase in expenses / expense-reduction efforts: **−¥190.0 bn**
- Other: **−¥242.6 bn**
- **Total: −¥102.6 bn**

So FX gains (+345) and marketing (+70) were more than offset by cost inflation and higher expenses/other (−517.6 combined). At the segment level, Automotive operating income fell 21.0% to ¥719.9 bn on "increased expenses and others," while Financial Services rose 24.0% to ¥275.6 bn.

**The bridge from −¥102.6 bn operating income to +¥711.7 bn pre-tax income:**
- Non-operating income: **+¥814.3 bn** — the dominant driver (other income jumped from ¥86.0 bn to ¥900.3 bn)
- Share of profit of equity-method investments: **+¥69.6 bn**
- Total below-the-line swing: **+¥883.9 bn**, which more than covers the operating decline

So the strong net income gain came almost entirely from non-operating/other income (e.g., interest and other non-operating items, valuation/financial gains) plus equity-method income — not from Toyota's core vehicle business, which was pressured by expenses and costs despite favorable FX tailwinds.

**Sources:**
- Toyota FY2027 Q1 Financial Summary (official): https://global.toyota/pages/global_toyota/ir/financial-results/2027_1q_summary_en.pdf
- Toyota Form 6-K FY2027 Q1 (SEC): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1094517/000119312526331392/d258414dex991.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1094517/000119312526331392/d258414dex992.htm
- Toyota Times FY2027 1Q results: https://toyotatimes.jp/en/toyota_news/financial_results_2027/001.html
- StockTitan summary of the 6-K: https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/TM/6-k-toyota-motor-corp-current-report-foreign-issuer-bc5b6a9ae3a4.html
- Just Auto: https://www.just-auto.com/news/toyota-raises-guidance-net-income
- WardsAuto: https://www.wardsauto.com/news/toyota-sees-north-american-profitability-targets-cost-savings-in-hybrids/827022
